decision: fanned out 11 read-only research agents over tC4 code, docs, PR 688, Door43, Pankosmia, Burrito schema, Aquifer, UI tech, merge tech

decision: user is very happy with tC4's UI and its design system, so the rebuild keeps them: same screens, tokens, components and look

decision: do not reuse pankosmia-web; build our own Rust storage and sync core; port Proskomma's versification mapper
why: pankosmia-web is binary-only (no usable lib API), writes are not crash-safe, metadata rewrites drop fields, its merge writes conflict markers into files, it has no working tests, and 0.19.2 breaks commits after the first

decision: the rebuild must open projects made by tC4 4.0 (one-file-per-action journal, checking/ sidecars) through an importer, not by copying that format byte for byte
why: pilots start using tC4 4.0 on Oct 16 and their work must carry over; byte-identical regeneration would need JavaScript key ordering and usfm-js text quirks, which is the wrong thing to bind a new core to

decision: probed egui/eframe 0.36 (user offered it): epaint 0.36.2 shapes with harfrust but has no bidi; Hebrew and Arabic come out left-to-right (reversed); no Graphite shaper either
why: the vision makes correct rendering of the user's writing system an invariant and tC4 ships an RTL journey, so the UI stack must pass an RTL test before it is chosen

decision: adopted tC4's silent-loss cases as must-pass merge tests: concurrent verse bridges, edit to a verse a teammate merged away, stale whole-book save, clock-skew wins, Door43 web edits, two machines with one identity, one bad file blocking sync
why: the research reproduced each against tC4's reference fold; the rebuild's merge must turn every one into a visible conflict or a lossless merge

decision: validate every written burrito in Rust with jsonschema (no network features) against the SB v1.0.0 schema bundle, plus code checks the schema misses (languages present, path rules, md5/size match bytes, scope books covered)
why: probe matched ajv on 48 of 48 broken samples and both tC4 samples pass; develop-branch schema is an unreleased draft that rejects OBS

decision: UI architecture: Rust core served on localhost to a Rust-compiled-to-WASM web UI that reuses tC4's CSS, tokens and fonts; Electronite is the production shell, any Chromium/browser works for dev and tests
why: only Electronite has proven Graphite; system webviews fail Graphite on all three OSes (WebKitGTK drops vertical offsets), egui fails RTL; reusing the CSS gives the UI the user likes; Playwright can drive it in CI
result: decided, framework (Dioxus vs Leptos) still open

decision: Aquifer enters as a second helps source: pinned GitHub release zips (tag + commit sha + asset sha256) converted into the same helps model the DCS loader fills; view-only tabs first, tN check later needs UGNT/UHB from DCS
why: Aquifer mirrors tN/tW/tA/tQ under CC BY-SA 4.0 in pinnable repos; its API needs a key and serves a different database; tW has no original words so cannot drive a check

why: the UI framework is a one-way door for ~60 screens and the owner wants the current look; a measured prototype beats a guess

decision: rejected CRDT libraries and git's own merge for project content; git2 moves bytes only, gix ruled out (cannot push)

why: the storage format is the riskiest one-way door; independent designs plus adversarial review beat one design defended by its author
